name: Artemis I — Distant Retrograde Orbit
description: Artemis I, 16 Nov – 11 Dec 2022: SLS/Orion launch, trans-lunar injection, the outbound powered flyby, a six-day distant retrograde orbit about the Moon, the return flyby, and Pacific splashdown.

tracks.SOURCE: JPL Horizons 301 (Moon), center 500@399, geocentric ICRF (reference plane FRAME), DE441, VEC_CORR=NONE, over 2022-11-04..2022-12-11 at a 900 s grid, including a 0.45-lunar-period pre-roll before launch for the ADR-0006 trail window. The Moon and Orion are the only real, cited positions; no genuine Artemis I state vectors exist.

RECONSTRUCTED (Phase 1: launch to TLI start). SLS Block 1 ascent (4xRS-25 + 2 SRB) propagates with a two-phase gravity-turn thrust profile fitted to SRB sep at 000:00:02:12 and MECO at 000:00:08:03; the ICPS then circularises into a parking orbit, raises the orbit at 000:00:52:56, and coasts to the 000:01:29:27 TLI epoch. Pad latitude 28.5 N is a free parameter (untextured Earth). Positions/velocities are solved to the published MET anchors, not telemetry.
